Since $\alpha \in \left(\pi, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$, $\dfrac{\alpha}{2} \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)$, where the cosine is negative and the tangent is negative. Then $\cos^2\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{1 + \cos\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{9}{25}$, so $\cos\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = -\dfrac{3}{5}$, and $\tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{1 + \cos\alpha} = -\dfrac{4}{3}$.
form: sin α given in QII-QIV → the correct pair cos(α/2), tan(α/2)
